## What is `frontend/.next`?
The `.next` folder is the **build output directory** that Next.js automatically creates when you run `npm run dev` or `npm run build`.
---
### Think of it like this:
``` Your code (src/) → npm run build → .next/ (what you write) (compilation) (what the browser runs) ```
---
### What's inside `.next/`:
| Folder | What it contains | |---|---| | `.next/cache/` | Cached files to make builds faster | | `.next/server/` | Server-side rendered pages | | `.next/static/` | CSS, JavaScript bundles for the browser | | `.next/types/` | Auto-generated TypeScript types |
---
### Key facts:
**You never edit it** — it's auto-generated, always overwritten by Next.js
**It's in `.gitignore`** — it should never be pushed to GitHub ``` frontend/.next/ ← already ignored in your project ```
**It gets recreated** every time you run: ```bash npm run dev # development mode npm run build # production mode ```
**You can safely delete it** and it will be rebuilt: ```bash rm -rf frontend/.next cd frontend && npm run dev ```
---
### Simple analogy:
Your TypeScript/React source code (`.tsx` files) is like a **recipe written in English**.
The `.next` folder is the **cooked meal** — the browser can't read TypeScript directly, so Next.js compiles it into plain JavaScript that browsers understand, and stores that in `.next/`.
